stave-line.note: Resolves to #868988 over score stock — 3.05:1. Level systems only; the engraved hero system draws its staff lines in printing ink at 0.85 opacity.

display.purpose: The work title, once per page, at score title-block position.

headline.purpose: Section headings beside their rehearsal mark; capped 20-22ch.

voice.purpose: Display italic. Tempo indication, Mây's margin notes, and the 'who this level is for' line. Italic means a person is speaking.

body.purpose: Running text, capped at the 66ch measure.

label.purpose: Uppercase 0.14em label used inline only — composer-position role, level ordinal. Never stacked above a heading as a kicker.

music.purpose: Bravura SMuFL codepoints. Real glyphs only, font-display: block.

shadows.name: lift-1
shadows.purpose: The primary action at rest. The only shadow on a resting element anywhere in the build.

shadows.name: lift-2
shadows.purpose: The primary action on hover, paired with a 1px rise.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Every state transition and the margin-note entrance use it.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Control hover: background, colour, border-colour, transform, box-shadow.

motion.name: write-in
motion.purpose: The one authored moment — margin notes fade and rise 6px on intersection at 0.55 threshold, once each. Fully collapsed and pre-revealed under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Action (CTA)
components.description: The one filled red control per passage. Nothing else on the page may take a red fill.
components.html: Chọn cấp độ của bạn
components.css: .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem; padding: 0.85rem 1.5rem; background: var(--edit, #a32b22); color: var(--paper, #edefea); font-family: var(--face-text, 'Be Vietnam Pro', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(18,21,26,.07), 0 6px 16px -10px rgba(18,21,26,.22); transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-cta svg { transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-cta:hover { background: #8d221a; transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgba(18,21,26,.08), 0 18px 40px -22px rgba(18,21,26,.4); } .ds-cta:hover svg { transform: translateX(3px); } .ds-cta:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-cta:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--edit, #a32b22); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 1px; }

components.name: Pending Bracket
components.description: The engraver's mark on an unresolved passage. Marks every slot awaiting the owner's real material, and is deliberately quieter than any adjacent control.

components.name: Outcome Chip

components.name: Level System (structural stave)
components.description: Five hairlines as a repeating gradient (1.2px on a 9px period), so they stay crisp at any width and can span a whole row. Opens each level row and is the only separator between levels.

components.name: Final Barline
components.description: A score ends on a thin-then-thick final barline, so the page does too. Drawn as SVG at the same 10-unit staff space as the engraved system.
components.css: .ds-close { display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 420px; height: auto; color: rgba(223,231,225,.4); } .ds-close__line { fill: currentColor; opacity: 0.85; }

narrative.overview:
The page is set on the stave rather than decorated with music. Everything the surface knows how to do it learned from music engraving: a title block that puts the work title, the tempo indication and the composer's line where a printed score puts them; five-line systems that carry content instead of framing it; rehearsal marks that name places so a teacher can say 'from B'; a coda that closes on a thin-then-thick final barline. Notation is set in real SMuFL glyphs from Bravura, never in unicode look-alikes, and the notation font loads with font-display: block so a stave never flashes a letterform.

The density is that of a printed page, not an app: flat cool stock, ink hierarchy carried by three greys rather than by boxes, and almost no borders that are not either a stave, a rehearsal-mark box, or a control outline. Depth is essentially absent — one soft two-layer lift exists and it belongs to a single control. Colour is rationed hard: the whole surface is ink on paper except three whole-field passages (the evening room, the press-green coda, the gathered student stock) and one saturated red that means act or the teacher is speaking.

Vietnamese is a hard typographic constraint, not a locale setting. Both text faces were chosen for full Vietnamese coverage first and character second, because Vietnamese stacks two diacritic tiers and a face missing them falls back to the system font on exactly those glyphs — a break only a Vietnamese reader sees. All three faces are self-hosted, subset, and preloaded; there is no CDN anywhere in the critical path.
keyCharacteristics: Ink on cool stock (#EDEFEA), never cream, never white
One action colour, rationed to a single filled control per passage
Zero corner radius on every surface and control
Five-line staves as structure, not ornament
Real notation glyphs; inline SVG for the two UI icons
One authored motion moment on the whole page

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Saturated red is a fill on exactly one control per passage — the primary action. Everywhere else it may only be a hairline, an underline, a focus ring, a hover state, or the teacher's own italic hand. A second red-filled control on a screen is a bug.

rules.name: The Bracket Is Not A Button Rule
rules.body: Slots awaiting the owner's real material are set in the pending family — ink type (#3a4048), a warm grey bracket stroke (#8e8079), and a 4.5%-opacity wash — precisely so an unfinished passage can never out-shout the action next to it. Never promote a pending bracket to the action colour.

rules.name: The Whole-Field Rule
rules.body: Press green is a field or a glyph fill. It never becomes a border, a divider, or a hairline.

rules.name: The Italic Is A Voice Rule
rules.body: Display italic is reserved for someone speaking to the reader. If nobody is talking, it is not italic.

rules.name: The Tight-Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is set at weight 800 with negative tracking that increases with size (−0.012em at title, −0.022em at headline, −0.04em at display). Never letterspace the serif open.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The uppercase 0.14em label exists only inline, on the baseline row of the thing it qualifies. It is never stacked above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow, and never used as a section label.

rules.name: The Real-Glyph Rule
rules.body: Musical symbols are Bravura codepoints, never unicode stand-ins, never an image. Adding a symbol means re-cutting the subset; an uncut codepoint renders as nothing by design.

rules.name: The Vietnamese-First Rule
rules.body: Any face added to this system must carry the full Vietnamese diacritic set and be self-hosted with unicode-range subsets. Coverage decides before character does.

rules.name: The Stave Is The Grid Rule
rules.body: Where a row needs separating from the next, it opens on a five-line system. The stave is the divider; nothing else divides anything. Never draw a plain rule directly above a stave — at ink weight it reads as a sixth, wrong staff line.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Paragraphs are capped at 66ch by default and headings at 20–24ch. A full-bleed line of text is out of world.

rules.name: The One Lifted Thing Rule
rules.body: Only the primary action carries a shadow. Cards, panels, media wells and pending brackets stay flat on the sheet; separate them with tone or a stave instead.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0 on every surface and control. The only exceptions are the 1px focus ring and the scrollbar thumb.

rules.name: The Two Staves Rule
rules.body: Notation that must be read is SVG at SMuFL metrics with real glyphs. Structural staves that must span an arbitrary width are a repeating gradient. Never draw a readable system with a gradient, and never stretch an SVG system to fill a row.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The page has one authored motion moment: the teacher's margin notes write themselves in on intersection (700ms, opacity plus a 6px rise, once each), plus notehead highlighting during playback. Everything else is a 140–180ms state transition on a control. prefers-reduced-motion collapses all of it and reveals the notes immediately.

rules.name: The Claimed-Surfaces Rule
rules.body: Browser defaults belong to no design system, so this one claims them: selection, caret, accent-color, scrollbar track and thumb, focus ring, and link underline offset (0.22em) and colour. Numerals that sit in columns take tabular-nums.

dos: Do open a new row or section on a five-line system and let it do the dividing.
Do keep the saturated red to one filled control per passage; use ink outlines for every secondary action.
Do set anything the owner still owes as a pending bracket, in the pending ink family, with a bold-italic phrase naming exactly what is missing.
Do use real Bravura codepoints for musical symbols and re-cut the subset when you add one.
Do check any new text colour against its actual ground and record the ratio next to the token, as --ink-3 (5.34:1) and --focus-dark (7.5:1 on the room) already do.
Do substitute the dark-passage focus colour inside the evening room; editor's red is only ~2.7:1 there.
Do give every interactive control a 44px minimum target, growing the hit area around a small printed mark rather than inflating the mark.
Do cap paragraphs at the 66ch measure and headings at 20–24ch.
Do self-host any new face with unicode-range subsets and full Vietnamese coverage.
donts: Don't round a corner. Radius is 0 except the 1px focus ring and the scrollbar thumb.
Don't add a shadow to anything but the primary action, and never a zero-offset halo or a hard offset shadow.
Don't build cards. Group with tone, spacing and staves.
Don't let a pending bracket, a chip, or a price note take the action colour.
Don't use press green for a hairline, border or divider.
Don't stack an uppercase tracked label above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow; that label only ever sits inline beside its partner.
Don't use a unicode character, an emoji, or an icon font where a notation glyph belongs — and use inline SVG, not a glyph font, for UI icons.
Don't scatter hover reveals or entrance animations; the page has one authored motion moment and the budget is spent.
Don't load a font from a CDN.
Don't reintroduce the course-landing furniture this world refuses: instructor hero, benefit columns, testimonial cards, pricing table, FAQ accordion.
